question.prompt: Let \(ABCDEF\) be a regular hexagon with side length \(1.\) Denote by \(X,\) \(Y,\) and \(Z\) the midpoints of sides \(AB,\) \(CD,\) and \(EF,\) respectively. What is the area of the convex hexagon whose interior is the intersection of the interiors of \(\triangle ACE\) and \(\triangle XYZ?\)

solutions.title: Subtract three corner triangles
solutions.explanation:
The intersection can be found by removing three congruent corner triangles from \(\triangle XYZ\). We first determine the size of one corner.

Let \(O\) be the hexagon's center. Joining \(O\) to the vertices produces six equilateral triangles of side \(1\), so \(BE=2\). Also, \(AF=1\) and \(AF\parallel BE\).

To find \(XZ\), let \(T\) be the midpoint of \(AE\). The triangle midsegment theorem in \(\triangle ABE\) and \(\triangle AEF\) gives
\[
XT=\frac{BE}{2}=1,
\qquad TZ=\frac{AF}{2}=\frac12.
\]
These segments form the straight segment \(XZ\), so \(XZ=\frac32\) and \(XZ\parallel BE\). Rotation through \(120^\circ\) cycles \(X,Y,Z\), so \(\triangle XYZ\) is equilateral with side \(\frac32\).

Define \(U=AC\cap XZ\) and \(V=AC\cap XY\). In isosceles triangle \(ABC\), the angle at \(B\) is \(120^\circ\), so \(\angle BAC=30^\circ\). Its symmetry line \(BE\) is perpendicular to \(AC\), and thus \(XZ\perp AC\).

Consequently, \(\triangle AXU\) is right at \(U\), with a \(60^\circ\) angle at \(X\). Triangle \(VXU\) is also right at \(U\), and its angle at \(X\) is \(60^\circ\) because \(XYZ\) is equilateral. These two triangles share \(XU\) and have matching angles, so they are congruent. Therefore
\[
XV=AX=\frac12,
\qquad XU=\frac14,
\qquad UV=\sqrt{\left(\frac12\right)^2-\left(\frac14\right)^2}
=\frac{\sqrt3}{4}.
\]
The corner triangle \(XUV\) has area
\[
\frac12\cdot\frac14\cdot\frac{\sqrt3}{4}
=\frac{\sqrt3}{32}.
\]
Side \(AC\) cuts off this corner of \(XYZ\), and sides \(CE\) and \(EA\) cut off its rotated copies at \(Y\) and \(Z\). On each side of \(XYZ\), the two removed corner portions have total length \(\frac12+\frac14<\frac32\), so the corner triangles are disjoint. Their removal leaves exactly the required intersection hexagon.

An equilateral triangle of side \(s\) has area \(\frac{\sqrt3}{4}s^2\). The requested area is therefore
\[
\frac{\sqrt3}{4}\left(\frac32\right)^2
-3\left(\frac{\sqrt3}{32}\right)
=\frac{9\sqrt3}{16}-\frac{3\sqrt3}{32}
=\boxed{\frac{15\sqrt3}{32}}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\text{C}\).
